title: Feature: Add support for vision estimate feed
body: This would be a good enhancement for more complex systems

comments.body: @TSC21 can you please give some more details what exactly is needed here. What data and functionality needs to be exposed? What are the underlying mavlink messages?

Sure thing. So the idea would be to interface this with using fast-RTPS as the Pub/Sub framework. A direct OpenCV visual odometry plugin could be written and be taken as an example, but wouldn't actually serve as an interface, but rather as an idea of how OpenCV could be integrated in a visual odometry pipeline.
The underlying Mavlink msgs would be `VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE` (for pose), `VISUAL_SPEED_ESTIMATE` (for velocity) and `ODOMETRY`, which gives a more complete visual odometry msg.
I mean `fast-RTPS/RabbitMQ/etc. -> SDK -> mavlink -> autopilot`, since you will be sending the VIO data to the autopilot, not getting from it.
Ok got it. In this case the SDK does not need to implement any of `fast-RTPS/RabbitMQ/etc` but only provide the API for mavlink which makes sense.

> In this case the SDK does not need to implement any of `fast-RTPS/RabbitMQ/etc` but only provide the API for mavlink which makes sense.

Partially. I mean, if you want to subscribe to published VIO data in the `RabbitMQ` framework, you need to add an handler for that data, right? Creating a transparent agnostic class that handles the subscriptions to these brokers may make sense. Then, the vision plugin would get the data from that interface.
Let me know if you are interested to tackle this together.

> Let me know if you are interested to tackle this together.

I can try to help you if you have questions but I need to work on a couple of other things first like integration tests in CI and the Java wrapper first.
There is support for VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE in the Mocap plugin.

title: Example Fly mission uses hard-coding of mission points
body:
Fly mission example uses[ hard-coding](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/example/fly_mission/fly_mission.cpp#L73) of waypoints. It is hard for someone to compute longitude, latitude, etc and use this example.
I prefer, we can make this example take QGC Mission plan as input; where one can plan missions using QGC and feed its path via command-line to this example.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26615772/31763673-972c5bb6-b4dc-11e7-8ff0-f8b39b6b88c3.png)


We can parse QGC mission plan and pass mission items to DroneCore Mission plugin.
Make sense ?

Regards,
Shakthi

comments.body:
Thanks for the issue. This has been requested several times actually and it would be a good thing to have.

The only catch is that not all mission items are currently supported in DroneCore, so we won't be fully compatible. We would have to just ignore unsupported items and warn the user about it.

@julianoes @shakthi-prashanth-m 

> Fly mission example uses hard-coding of waypoints. It is hard for someone to compute longitude, latitude, etc and use this example.

The solution to this problem is NED based mission points - as per #100.
I really think it makes sense to implement this ourselves, sooner rather than later.

> The only catch is that not all mission items are currently supported in DroneCore, so we won't be fully compatible. We would have to just ignore unsupported items and warn the user about it.

My take on this is that mission import should completely bypass whatever we do with the API. It would be something to add flexibility over the top of our existing API. So perhaps:
- Allow upload and download of files *or strings* in generic waypoint format. Users can then dynamically construct the messages if they want.
- Provide an API to send a generic waypoint message or custom message - so the user can send whatever message they like. 

Yes I know it removes some of the "clean-ness" of the API, but if we don't do this then I personally as a user would be forced to write my own plugin to do this.

@shakthi-prashanth-m So what does https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/121#issuecomment-364714307 add to this discussion? 

I still think we should implement #100

> @shakthi-prashanth-m So what does #121 (comment) add to this discussion?

@hamishwillee, sorry which comment ? The link you referred says that **you opened this on Oct 20, 2017**! :-)

>I still think we should implement #100

Yeah, I think this is useful too. So I [added my question](https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/100#issuecomment-364835706) regarding NED mission for my understanding.
@shakthi-prashanth-m I was asking about why you added #235 to this discussion. I've responded re NED missions.
Yeah, because this issue was about complexity of user's effort in uploading mission with hard-coding waypoint alt, lon. As #235 deals this indirectly, I referenced it.

title: ArduPilot/other mavlink autopilot compatiblity/support
body:
Hello, 

Do you plan to open compatibility/support for other mavlink based autopilot like ardupilot ?
Will you accept a PRs in that objectifs ?

comments.body: That would be real nice IMO !

We would love to support other MAVLink autopilots, but:
1. Our main priority is rock solid performance on Dronecode platform. 
2. We don't have time or resources to maintain the port.

So the short answer is yes, but only if the person making the contributions commits to maintaining them and helps to put in place the infrastructure needed to test them. 

As an aside I think that as long as the `DroneCore` and `Device` classes work OK with another autopilot, the new architecture would give us lots of choices about how we might support said autopilot in the plugins.

@julianoes Is that a fair assessment of our position?

title: Add Avoidance Plugin to MAVSDK
body:
These are my first thoughts regarding adding an avoidance plugin to MAVSDK.

Requirements: In my mind, as per the rest of MAVSDK, this plugin should be self-contained and therefore not depend on any other frameworks such as ROS. In fact, I don't think that the core Avoidance plugin should even implement any actual avoidance logic; it should just expose a high level API to the [MAVLink Path Planning (Trajectory) protocol](https://mavlink.io/en/services/trajectory.html). This will allow for a flexible way to implement Mission mode obstacle avoidance - see [PX4 Obstacle Avoidance](https://docs.px4.io/v1.9.0/en/computer_vision/obstacle_avoidance.html) for more details. If any avoidance logic for i.e. point cloud via LiDAR is implemented, it should be kept separate.

The two main architectures that come to mind for me are:

1. A "polling" approach - the user calls avoidance.receive_trajectory() which returns a list of waypoints. These waypoints are then altered as needed to "avoid obstacles". Finally, avoidance.upload_trajectory() is called on the new waypoints. This procedure is repeated in a loop at 5Hz.
2. A "subscribing" approach - the avoidance API allows you to subscribe a function as a callback. The existing trajectory is passed into the callback, processed, then outputted in the function return. In this approach, MAVSDK handles registering and triggering the callback, and the user only implements the callback.

Off the bat, the subscribing approach seems cleaner to me. However, there are a few considerations to make before deciding on and implementing an approach:
- Although I'm not sure if it will be performant enough, I would like to leave room for writing gRPC bindings for other languages.
- If considering other languages bindings, callbacks might be implemented differently, so this will have to be figured out.
- Callbacks require the avoidance logic function to be somewhat contained, and if other variables/code are required, it might be hard to reference other code. I'm not sure to what extent this is a problem, as I haven't done much async/callbacks in C++ before.

I'd love to hear people's thoughts to decide on an architecture, so I can start developing it!

title: server plugins should not be limited to a single system
body:
As I have been working on the camera server plugin, I've noticed a problem with the way the current plugin architecture creates a plugin instance per system (i.e. `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(System& system) : PluginImplBase(system)`). The problem is that the plugin state is per system when really it needs to be global. This means that consumers of MAVSDK have to do lots of extra work to ensure that each plugin instance for a single camera remains in a consistent state with the others. Example: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1699/commits/1528f0cf05fcae55be6941694f7d935d0fa378b0.

I suppose other server plugins haven't noticed this problem before since they probably only communicate with one system. However, cameras need to communicate with both an autopilot and a ground station at the same time.

I think a solution to this would be to create a new "server" plugin type that is initialized with `CameraServerImpl::CameraServerImpl(Mavsdk& mavsdk) : ServerPluginImplBase(mavsdk)` instead. Then a single plugin instance could receive and send messages to any number of systems. (And broadcast to multiple systems as required by [CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#CAMERA_IMAGE_CAPTURED).)

Otherwise, we should reconsider https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/274#issuecomment-1039591231, particularly the `Set*` methods. Basically, the camera server plugin should have no state and everything is handled by callbacks to user code. I'm not sure this is really possible though since the callbacks themselves are considered part of the state.

title: Provided MAVLink headers are installed to the wrong directory
body:
When supplying MAVLink C-header files and building from source, the build system installs the headers to a location that's not able to be found by `mavlink_include.h`.

Ubuntu 18.04 LTS
CMake v3.24.3

Configuration:
`cmake -B build/default -S . -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=all -DMAVLINK_HEADERS=../my_headers -H.`

Build and Install:
`sudo cmake --build build/default --target install -j8`

Resulting directory structure:
`/usr/local/include/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/**my_headers**/mavlink/v2.0/...`

Include line from `mavlink_passthrough/mavlink_include.h`:
`#include "mavlink/v2.0/all/mavlink.h`

---

To fix this, I edited `mavsdk/src/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough/CMakeLists.txt`:
```
install(DIRECTORY
    ${MAVLINK_HEADERS} --> ${MAVLINK_HEADERS}/mavlink
    DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/mavsdk/plugins/mavlink_passthrough
)
```

title: Changing mode to GUIDED
body:
Hi,
I ran the takeoff_and_land example.
In some cases it did not takeoff. Now, I figured out that this was because the arducopter wasn't in GUIDED mode.
What can be the easiest way to command it to GUIDED mode ?

comments.body:
[Here is](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387) the ardupilot implementation of the takeoff. My understanding is that if it is not in GUIDED mode (which MAVSDK calls "offboard"), then it should set it to GUIDED and then takeoff.

Which version of MAVSDK are you using?
libmavsdk-dev_1.4.6_ubuntu20.04_amd64.deb

Oh, it is fixed in the main branch (which will become MAVSDK v2 at some point), but not in the v1.4.13 branch (which is the latest release): https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4.13/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp.

So you have two solutions:
1. Build MAVSDK from source from the main branch, so that you get the fix
2. Open a PR backporting the fix from main to the v1.4 branch, and then we could make a v1.4.14 release

I don't know how many similar fixes are in `main` and not in `v1.4` (apparently `v1.4` is currently 438 commits behind `main`: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/v1.4). If I was using Ardupilot, I would personally build MAVSDK from source to make sure I don't miss other similar fixes.

But that's your choice :blush:.

I would suggest to use the main branch for building the library as well since there are many Ardupilot related changes which are not in the latest release. Closing for now, please reopen if the issue persists with the main branch as well.

Hello, I know this issue is closed but I'd like to add to it and perhaps suggest that it is reopened... I have changed to main branch, built from source etc. and the `takeoff` MavSDK action does work now... sometimes. I have been using the ArduPilot SITL environment to test my code and have noticed that I sometimes get a seg fault when using the `takeoff` command. I have tried out quite a few things and I *think* I have boiled it down to the `takeoff` command switching to `GUIDED` mode when there is no `position` as outlined in the logs shown in the image below. Based on [action.h](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/48f1ad0325ecdcb8075d7ffd0cd7a8323af12fb3/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/include/plugins/action/action.h#L84), I am getting a takeoff response of 13 which relates to `Failed` as shown below: ```cpp enum class Result { Unknown, /**< @brief Unknown result. */ Success, /**< @brief Request was successful. */ NoSystem, /**< @brief No system is connected. */ ConnectionError, /**< @brief Connection error. */ Busy, /**< @brief Vehicle is busy. */ CommandDenied, /**< @brief Command refused by vehicle. */ CommandDeniedLandedStateUnknown, /**< @brief Command refused because landed state is unknown. */ ...[truncated]

Hi Oliver, thanks for reporting the issue. Could you maybe try by changing the takeoff code in your local MAVSDK to switch to Stabilize flight mode instead of guided mode before takeoff? Please check it on SITL ;) Relevant code is here.

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/48f1ad0325ecdcb8075d7ffd0cd7a8323af12fb3/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387

Stabilize mode does not need position so should not create this particular issue:
https://ardupilot.org/copter/docs/stabilize-mode.html#stabilize-mode

What is your use-case? You would need position fix anyways before carrying out an auto mission right? In such a case waiting for a good fix before activating takeoff should be prudent. Or are you flying indoors?

Arducopter allows to takeoff in a selected number of flight modes out of which Guided was selected since MAVSDK is supposed to control the drone from such a mode. But I am open to discussing this further to find the best suitable mode for takeoff for most scenarios. Would also discuss this with the ArduPilot Dev team shortly.

body:
~~From my experience, MAVSDK does not detect a system is lost on soft reboot. Which is fine for most things I am doing. camera_server, param, and mavlink_passthrough seem to work fine for me even after the soft reboot.~~

~~The problem is that gimbal does not work after the reboot. Giving any gimbal control after soft rebooting will result in a failure to do so, with it returning the result as "Error". ~~

~~My assumption is that MAVSDK still thinks it has control of the gimbal, when it doesn't, since it did not know the autopilot was rebooted. I am not able to make it so that MAVSDK detects reboots, even if I increase BRD_BOOT_DELAY. 
In my application, this will be fine, because I have a background thread that detects when we last received telemetry position, so I can use that to detect a reboot, but I still wanted to make an issue here, just to give a heads up of the issue I found.~~



System:

MAVSDK v3.2.0
ArduCopter 4.5.6
Pixy LR gimbal

Note: MAVSDK is connected to flight controller via UART



**Edit:**

I fixed this issue. The problem was not due to rebooting.

The Pixy LR gimbal sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 154 and the autopilot sends GIMBAL_MANAGER messages from comp id 1. I hard coded MAVSDK to completely ignore comp id 154 and the intermittent problem is gone. 

As a note, it would constantly request GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION from 1/154. I know MAVSDK has a retries mechanism, but it didn't seem to stop this. So my hardcoding got rid of that.

I want to add a few custom mavlink messages for my own dialect, not part of upstream, and develop without having to commit and push to a repository.

Then, for a local build, mavlink is built and installed, so that its config file is on disk.
This allows it to be found through find_package:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L4

For some reason, regardless of the setting for the MAVLINK_DIALECT, it does not get affect the command here:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5b66d5fb8e2032b9f24dc08867e950b0b32ec82e/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt#L27-L39


I want to

* Add a new local mavlink XML dialect, say my_custom.xml
* Get MAVSDK to also generate that dialect in addition to the normal dialect
* Use those new messages to send custom packets via mavsdk

Can we either document or add support for mavlink to be brought in through a submodule, fetchcontent, or how to build/install mavlink on the system that does not rely on merging stuff upstream first? Perhaps we can support a way where mavlink on the system can be used.

In mavlink:
```
cmake -B build -DMAVLINK_DIALECT=MyCustomDialect
cmake --build build
cmake --install build --prefix install

```
Then, when building MAVSDK, perhaps we can allow a user to add "/path/to/mavlink/install" to the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH and use that version instead of pulling from upstream.
